=== Morphological Assessment Form ===
A. Leaf Arrangement & Architecture
    1. Leaf relative position (alternate / opposite / whorled): opposite (pairs of compound leaves are visible at successive nodes along the stem)
    2. Leaf spacing (clustered / distal): clustered (leaves are grouped closely together at the apex of the seedling)
B. Leaf Complexity
    3. Leaf complexity (simple / compound): compound (each leaf unit is composed of multiple leaflets)
    4. Compound leaf type, ONLY if leaf complexity is compound (odd-pinnate / even-pinnate): odd-pinnate (each leaf has a single terminal leaflet at the end of the rachis)
    5. Number of leaflets (integer estimate 2, 4, 8, …): 5 (clearly visible on multiple leaves)
    6. Leaflet arrangement (opposite / alternate / subopposite): alternate (leaflets are arranged alternately along the rachis, with the terminal leaflet)
C. Leaf Morphology
    7. Leaf margin (entire / toothed) AND if toothed (dentate, serrate, etc.): entire (margins are smooth, though some leaves show mechanical damage/holes)
    8. Leaf shape (elliptic, obovate, lanceolate, etc.): obovate to elliptic (leaflets are broadly shaped, wider towards the apex)
    9. Leaf apex (acute, obtuse, acuminate): acute (the tip of the leaflets comes to a distinct point)
    10. Leaf base (rounded, cordate, cuneate): rounded (the base of the leaflets appears broad and rounded)
    11. Venation type (pinnate / palmate / parallel): pinnate (a central midrib with secondary veins branching off)
    12. Secondary veins (visibility, spacing, number): clearly visible, prominent, arranged in a pinnate pattern curving towards the margin
    13. Leaf surface features (glabrous, shiny, dull, rugose): dull (surface appears matte rather than glossy)
    14. Leaf surface trichomes (present / absent): present (fine hairs are visible along the rachis and leaflet margins in close-up views)
D. Stem & Shoot Traits
    17. Stem type, may not be visible (woody / herbaceous): herbaceous (the stem appears green and soft, typical of a young seedling)
    18. Stem trichomes (present / absent): present (hairs are visible on the stem surface)
    19. Stem color: green
    20. Stem texture (smooth / ridged / lenticellate): smooth (no obvious ridges or lenticels visible)
E. Other Visible Seedling Traits
    21. Stipules, sometimes visible only in close-up images (present / absent): not observed (not clearly visible in the provided images)
    22. Latex, rarely visible but extremely diagnostic when present (present / not observed): not observed
    23. Pulvinus, for Fabaceae family only (present / absent): not observed (no clear pulvinus visible at the leaf base)
    24. Tendrils (present / absent): absent

F. Notes: Several leaflets exhibit irregular holes and margin damage, consistent with mechanical injury or herbivory. Some leaf surfaces show light-colored speckling or mottling.
